JUDGMENT

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- from the respondents, for the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 18-06-2018 at about 5.20 p.m., the petitioner was riding the bicycle from Railway Wheel Factory towards Puttenahalli, near Dariwala Glass House, Doddaballapura main road, Yelahanka, Bengaluru city, with due care and caution and observing all traffic rules and regulations.

At that time, the rider of scooter bearing No.
KA-02-JD-7599 came on the same road in a rash and negligent manner, with high speed, endangering to human life and dashed to the petitioner.

As a result of which,
the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Manasa Trinity Hospital, wherein he took first aid treatment and thereafter, he was shifted to M. S. Ramaiah Hospital, Bengaluru,
wherein he took further treatment as an indoor patient.
Earlier to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and he was student, studying 8th standard.

Due to the accidental injuries he was not attended the school about six months and concentrate on study and thereby he was put to great financial loss in addition to physical disablement loss of one year education carrier.
The Yelahanka Traffic Police have registered the case against the rider of the said scooter for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337 and 338 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% per annum.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 appeared through their counsels and filed their separate written statements.
4. The respondent No.1 in her written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
She has contended that, she is the owner of the scooter bearing No. KA-02-JD-7599.

On Abhijoy Joju vs Sheela.U on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181212201/
2 18-06-2018, herself and her husband came to Puttenahalli cross, her husband went to purchase bread to her children and she was just keeping the scooter in corner side of the Puttenahalli main road.
At that time, all of a sudden one boy coming from B.W.S.S.B. main road towards Puttenahalli dashed to her scooter.
For humanity grounds she shifted him to Manasa Hospital and after his parents came, she left the place and came to her house.
After some time, the police called her and took her signature on a blank paper in the police station and took her papers including the insurance copy of United India Insurance Co. Ltd.
As on the date of accident her scooter was insured.
Hence, she is not liable to pay the claim amount.

In view of above denials and contentions,
she has prayed for dismissal of the petition.
5. The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

It has contended that, the rider of the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective driving licence to ride the same and also was not having other necessary documents such as RC, FC and insurance as required by M.V. Act.

It has further contended that, the minor petitioner very negligently rode his bicycle and suddenly came in wrong direction and dashed to the parked scooter from opposite direction and caused accident.
As such the entire fault lies on the minor petitioner and not on the part of the scooter rider.

On the day of alleged accident, the scooter rider was not riding his scooter, but parked the same on the extreme left side of the road and her husband went to bakery for purchase of some bakery items.
It is further contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exaggerated.
It has denied the issuance of insurance policy in respect of scooter bearing No. KA-02-JD-7599 in favour of respondent No.1.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Section 158(6) of M.V. Act.
Further, it sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1 as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
In view of above denials and contentions, it prayed for dismissal of the petition.

6. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, she has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 18-06-2018 at about 5.20 p.m., due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the scooter bearing Reg.
No.KA-02-JD-7599 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?
7.
In order to prove his case, the petitioner has got examined his natural guardian/father as P.W.1 and got marked 11 documents as Ex.P.1 to 11.
Further, he has got examined himself as P.W.2 and closed his side.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 examined its Administrative Officer as R.W.1 and got marked 2 documents as Ex.R.1 and 2 and closed its side.
The respondents No.1 has not adduced any evidence on her behalf.

3 8.
I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record.

9. My findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 10. Issue No.1: It is specific case of the petitioner that, he was riding the bicycle from Railway Wheel Factory towards Puttenahalli, near Dariwala Glass House, Doddaballapura main road, Yelahanka,
Bengaluru city, with due care and caution and observing all traffic rules and regulations.
At that time the rider of scooter bearing No. KA-02-JD-7599 came on the same road in a rash and negligent manner, with high speed, endangering to human life and dashed to him.
As a result of which, he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Manasa Trinity Hospital, wherein he took first aid treatment and thereafter, he was shifted to M. S.
Ramaiah Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took further treatment as an indoor patient.

11. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has examined his natural guardian/father as P.W.1 and himself as P.W.2 by filing examination-in-chief affidavits and got marked total 11 documents as Ex.P.1 to 11.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is true copy of first information statement, Ex.P.3 is true copy of Spot Mahazar, Ex.P.4 is true copy of sketch, Ex.P.5 is true copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.6 is true copy of Sec.133 notice, Ex.P.7 is true copy of reply to Sec.133 notice, Ex.P.8 is true copy of M.V.A. report, Ex.P.9 is true copy of indemnity bond, Ex.P.10 is true copy of charge-sheet and Ex.P.11 is true copy of statement of one Manju.

12. On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 11, prima-facia it reveals that, on 18-06- 2018 at about 5.20 p.m., when the petitioner was riding the bicycle from Railway Wheel Factory towards Puttenahalli, near Dariwala Glass House, Doddaballapura main road, Yelahanka, Bengaluru city, the rider of scooter bearing No. KA-02-JD-7599 came on the same road in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to him.
As a result of which, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

The investigation officer in his final report has clearly stated that, on the alleged date, time and place of accident, due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-02-JD-7599 the said accident has taken place and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries on vital parts of his body.

Further, the Ex.P.3 spot mahazer and Ex.P4 sketch also clearly speaks that, the petitioner was proceeding on his bicycle towards the extreme left side of the 60 feet width Yallahanka-Doddaballapur main road and the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-03/EK-1914 came from the South side connecting road and dashed to the bicycle of petitioner.
13.
The P.W.1 & P.W.2 have reiterated the entire averments made in the petition in their examination-in- chief affidavit.

Thought, the respondents No.1 and 2 have specifically denied the said facts in their written statements and in the cross-examination of P.W.1 & 2, they have not produced any rebuttal evidence to disprove the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by Abhijoy Joju vs Sheela.U on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181212201/
4 the petitioner.

Further, the P.W.1 & P.W.2 have unequivocally denied the suggestion made by the learned counsel for respondent No.2 that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of bicycle by the petitioner and not due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-02-JD-7599.
Further, they have clearly denied the suggestion that, the petitioner himself has dashed to the parked motorcycle of the respondent No.1.

Though,
the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross- examined P.W.1 and 2 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from their mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of their evidence.

14. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.5 wound certificate, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident and he has suffered ellis fracture with respect to 11 (class-III), small lacerated wound over upper and lower lips, swelling present tenderness present and tenderness over right upper chest.
On the other hand, the respondents have not led any evidence to substantiate the contentions taken in their written statements.

In such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely held that, the respondents have failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-02-JD-7599 and there is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
15. Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.8, the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident.
When the accident was not due to the any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle, then it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to negligence of the rider of offending vehicle.

Further, the investigation officer has clearly stated in the final report, marked as Ex.P.10, that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-02-JD-7599.
There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents and even nothing is elicited in the cross- examination of P.W.1 and P.W.2 to show that,
there is no fault or negligence on the part of rider of offending motorcycle

. In such circumstances,
there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the negligence of the rider of offending vehicle, place, date and time of accident,
involvement of the offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

16. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held

SCC 635
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."

Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 18-06-2018 at about 5.20 p.m., near Dariwala Glass House, Doddaballapura main road, Yelahanka, Bengaluru City, due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-02-JD-7599.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
19. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has caused due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-02-JD-7599 and he has sustained small lacerated wounds over upper and lower lips, swelling + tenderness + ellis fracture with respect to 11 (class-III) and tenderness over right upper chest.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning,
future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.
But, the petitioner being the minor, the avocation and income are not required to be ascertained.
Whereas, in order to assess the compensation under rest of the heads, the petitioner has not furnished any documentary evidences to establish the same.
In such circumstances, there is no other option but only to consider global compensation in general.

20. As per Ex.P.5 - wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained small lacerated wounds over upper and lower lips, swelling + tenderness + ellis fracture with respect to 11 (class-III) and tenderness over right upper chest.
The above said injury No.1 is grievous and injury No.2 is simple in nature.

The petitioner has deposed that, immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Manasa Trinity Hospital, wherein he took first aid treatment and thereafter, he was shifted to M. S. Ramaiah Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took further treatment as an indoor patient and he has spent Rs.50,000/- towards medicine, treatment, conveyance etc., and he has also spent Rs.10,000/-
towards conveyance.

Further he has deposed that, earlier to the accident he was hale and healthy and he was a student, studying in 8 th standard and due to the accidental injuries he had not attended the school for about six months and concentrate on study and thereby, he has put to great financial loss in addition to physical disablement and loss of one year education carrier.

But, it is pertinent to note that, the petitioner has neither examined the doctor, nor he has produced discharge summary, medical bills or any other document to show that he has taken treatment in the above said hospitals and has spent Rs.50,000/- towards medicine, treatment, conveyance etc., and Rs.10,000/- towards conveyance.

Such being the case, it is difficult to ascertain pain and sufferings,
laid up period, medical expenses, conveyance, amenities etc.
Further, there is absolutely no evidence placed on record to show that, the petitioner has suffered permanent disablement and deformity.

The petitioner being minor could have suffered some pain and sufferings, the same could have been nourished with nutritious food, attended with the attendants and might have spent for conveyance expenses.
Further, he might require some future medical expenses for ellis fracture sustained by him and in avoiding any deformity.

In such circumstances, taking into consideration the facts and circumstances of the case, even though there is no documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner, considering the wounds and pains suffered by the petitioner, on humanitarian ground Abhijoy Joju vs Sheela.U on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181212201/
6 and in general-globally, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioner should be awarded with some suitable compensation as he knocked the door of the temple of justice for compensation.
Accordingly, awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/- to the petitioner, would meet the ends of justice 21.
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.
KA-02-JD-7599 the accident has occurred.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damages caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.50,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization, from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
22. ISSUE No.3:

In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees fifty thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
The entire compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
